name: Edtech and online course businesses

problems.words: Webinar sign-ups are high but only a few buy
quick_ideas: Count sign-ups, attendees and buyers for the last webinar, so you see where people drop
Ask a few non-buyers why once, so you hear it in their words.

workzap_build.text: A funnel view from ad to sign-up to attendance to purchase, per webinar and course, updated daily.

problems.ask_first: Do most webinar sign-ups never attend, or do they attend and then not buy?
problems.free_stops: How the funnel stages are measured is kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the last webinar's questions, attendance drop points and buyer count, so you see where interest fades before purchase.
Give one person the job of noting buyer objections after each webinar, so your sales pitch gets fixed around real hesitations.

problems.words: Our sales team calls leads days late
quick_ideas: Check how long this week's leads waited for a first call, so the delay is measured
Give each new lead a named owner, so nobody assumes someone else called.

workzap_build.text: Leads routed to the sales team the moment they arrive, with speed alerts and call outcomes logged.

problems.ask_first: Do leads wait days for a call mostly at weekends, or throughout the week?
problems.free_stops: The routing and alert rules are in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many new leads sat untouched at each day part this week, so the slowest handoff period becomes obvious.
Keep one paper list of new leads beside the calling desk, so every caller works from the same queue.

problems.words: Card payments fail a lot for Pakistani learners
quick_ideas: List this month's failed payments by method, so you see which one fails
Offer a local alternative such as a wallet or bank transfer, so a failed card isn't a lost sale.

workzap_build.text: Local payment options connected alongside cards, with failed payments retried and followed up automatically.

problems.ask_first: Do card payments fail mostly at the payment step, or when the bank declines them?
problems.free_stops: The payment setup and retry flow are kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which course offers and times most often lead to failed card attempts, so patterns around Pakistani learner drop off appear.
Give one teammate the daily job of reviewing failed payment messages, so follow up stops being delayed or overlooked.

problems.words: Installment buyers stop paying after month two but keep access
quick_ideas: List overdue installment accounts today, so the size of it is clear
Decide your own rule for overdue access, so it's applied the same way.

workzap_build.text: Instalment reminders would go out by themselves, and course access would pause or return under your own rule.

problems.ask_first: Do instalment buyers stop in month two on most courses, or only on the costly ones?
problems.free_stops: The reminder and access rules are in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many overdue instalment learners still have access by course, so you see where unpaid seats are piling up.
Keep one overdue access list with one named owner for updates, so billing and access decisions stay aligned each week.

problems.words: Refund requests come through email, DMs and WhatsApp with no record
quick_ideas: Put every open refund request into one list, so none are missed or paid twice
Have one person decide them, so answers are consistent; for your obligations, talk to your lawyer.

workzap_build.text: A refund and chargeback register with reasons and access history for each case.

problems.ask_first: Do refund requests come mostly through WhatsApp, or are they spread across email and DMs?
problems.free_stops: The request flow and evidence kept per case are kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count open refund requests by channel and age on one page, so you see where delays and duplicate handling start.
Give one person one notebook for every refund request received, so scattered messages stop slipping past the team.

problems.words: Logins are shared — one account, many viewers
quick_ideas: Check which accounts were used from several places at once, so you know how big it is
Reset the accounts that stand out, so current sharing stops.

workzap_build.text: Sharing detection from login signals and per-account watermarking on videos, with alerts every day.

problems.ask_first: Is sharing mostly a few accounts used by many, or lots of accounts used by a few?
problems.free_stops: The detection signals are in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how often the same login appears active from different places on the same day, so the sharing pattern becomes visible.
Give one staff member the weekly review of unusual access notes, so follow up on shared logins happens consistently.

problems.words: Subscribers cancel after the first month
quick_ideas: Ask recent cancellers for their one main reason, so you know what to fix
Look at what new subscribers do in their first week, so you see who never really started.

workzap_build.text: customer_messaging — Churn tracked by cohort and reason, with first-week messages sent automatically to those who haven't started.

problems.ask_first: Do subscribers cancel after the first month mostly on one course, or across all of them?
problems.free_stops: The messages and churn reports are kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare what cancelled subscribers watched or attended in their opening days, so you see which starts fail to hook them.
Give one person the weekly cancellation reason list in one notebook, so retention fixes follow the same signals each time.

problems.words: Support is flooded with login problems
quick_ideas: Sort a week of support messages by topic, so you see which problems repeat
Write one clear help page for the top issue, so learners can fix it themselves.

workzap_build.text: WhatsApp support intake with automatic answers for login and access issues and response times measured.

problems.ask_first: Are login problems mostly forgotten passwords, or learners who cannot get in after paying?
problems.free_stops: The help flow and response targets are in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many support messages this week mention password reset, access link or wrong login, so the biggest blocker is clear.
Give one person the morning job of clearing login issues from one list, so simple cases stop clogging the support queue.

problems.words: Affiliates claim sales we can't verify
quick_ideas: Give each affiliate their own link or code from now on, so sales can be traced
Agree in writing what counts as a sale, so disputes have a rule.

workzap_build.text: Affiliate links and codes tracked to purchases, with monthly commission statements produced automatically.

problems.ask_first: Do affiliate claims come mostly from a few affiliates, or from most of them?
problems.free_stops: The tracking and statement setup are kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare claimed affiliate sales against your recorded enrolments by campaign period, so the disputed gap is clear before arguments grow.
Keep one written commission claims list with one owner updating it weekly, so affiliate questions are answered from the same record.

problems.words: LMS, payment gateway and CRM don't talk, so we copy-paste
quick_ideas: Write down every place your team copies the same data by hand from one tool to another, so you see the real load
Time one week of copying, so you know what it costs your team.

workzap_build.text: Each sale, refund and access change would show up in your course, payment and customer records at once, with no copy-pasting.

problems.ask_first: Which copying takes most time: sales into accounts, refunds, or access changes?
problems.free_stops: Which systems connect and how is set out in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many enrolment, payment and learner-status changes were retyped by staff since Monday, so the busiest break in the workflow shows.
Assign one staff member the midday update check and keep one paper list by the shared desk, so sales and course access stay aligned.

problems.words: I can't see revenue, refunds and churn per course in one place
quick_ideas: Choose the few numbers you want per course weekly, so the report has a shape
Pull them by hand once, so you see where each lives.

workzap_build.text: One screen with revenue, refunds, churn and ad spend per course and channel, updated daily.

problems.ask_first: Which is hardest to see per course: revenue, refunds or churn?
problems.free_stops: How the data is pulled together is kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Write each course on a page and note revenue, refunds and cancellations from this week, so weak courses stand out fast.
Give one person a fixed weekly time to update the course totals notebook, so the numbers arrive together for decisions.

never_say: Anything on data-protection or children's privacy law, app-store rules, consumer refund law, tax or fundraising; pi says "talk to your lawyer or accountant".
Help with dark patterns, fake countdowns, fake reviews or fake enrolment counters.
Income or job guarantees in course marketing.
Any idea that collects learners' names, emails, phones, logins, payments or progress, and nothing at all about children.
Help pirating content or covert tracking of learners' devices.
Visa or migration advice for immigration-linked courses.

sample_reply.person: Our biggest leak is shared accounts. One student buys, then the whole group logs in. What can we do?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this can be brought under control, and you can start today. 1) Check which accounts were used from several places at once, so you know how widespread it is. 2) Reset the accounts that stand out, so the current sharing stops. Workzap can do this automatically for you, spotting sharing every day and watermarking videos by account. Would you like me to arrange a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
